meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/05, Wednesday 7 June 2023), downloaded from www.ocr.org.uk. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded in the same sitting as OCR-JUN23-F-P2, its non-calculator Foundation partner. Interleaved crossover: J560/02 q20, q21, q24 and q25 reappear here as q4, q5, q7 and q10, marks matching item for item (3, 8, 5, 6 — 22 of the 100). 35 markers summing to exactly the printed 100.

coding_notes: q4, q5, q7 and q10 are J560/02 q20, q21, q24 and q25 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.
q5c is the outlier-identification pattern flagged across this audit; tagged scatter_graphs, consistent with its Foundation twin and with OCR-JUN24-F-P2 q22b.

q11 ('y is directly proportional to the square of x; find the percentage decrease in y') tagged proportion_with_powers then percentage_change. The mark scheme's whole route is squaring a multiplier, so direct_proportion alone would understate it.
q13b tagged exact_trig_values before pythagoras_theorem: the mark scheme awards a B1 purely for the exact value of sin 45, and the answer is required in exact simplified surd form.
q18 tagged fractional_and_negative_indices — the whole item is interpreting a fractional index, and the answer IS the index.
q20b tagged vector_proof rather than vectors: the required conclusion is that one vector is a multiple of another, so the points are collinear, and the accuracy mark depends on stating that.
